## Parent

[TIA-310: Upgrade Effect sources and native tooling to 4.0.1](<https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-310/upgrade-effect-sources-and-native-tooling-to-401>)

## What to build

Align the embedded Effect TypeScript-Go language service and its v4 fixtures with the stable Effect toolchain, using the native TypeScript 7 backend required by Effect-tsgo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The embedded Effect-tsgo package targets `@effect/tsgo@0.46.1`, tracked separately from Effect's synchronized 4.0.1 package versions.
- [ ] The v4 fixtures and their retained Node platform packages use Effect 4.0.1.
- [ ] The language service runs through the native TypeScript 7 backend while core package consumers retain the TypeScript 5.9 minimum.
- [ ] Effect language-service checks and fixture diagnostics pass against the stable APIs.

## Blocked by

* [TIA-311: Refresh the Effect source fork and dependency set to 4.0.1](<https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-311/refresh-the-effect-source-fork-and-dependency-set-to-401>).
planning_resolution_body:
## Decision resolution

The developer chose the stable Vite+ 1.0.0 rebase and working Effect fixes and suggestions through the Oxlint/Vite+ bridge. These choices complete the compatibility planning for [Upgrade Effect sources and native tooling to 4.0.1](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-310/upgrade-effect-sources-and-native-tooling-to-401), which remains the canonical implementation plan. Use its existing eight implementation tickets.

Detailed source evidence lives in the resolutions of [Establish the Effect 4.0.1 and Vitest 5 compatibility matrix](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-329/establish-the-effect-401-and-vitest-5-compatibility-matrix) and [Establish the native compiler and Effect lint compatibility matrix](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-330/establish-the-native-compiler-and-effect-lint-compatibility-matrix).

## Release and compatibility contract

- Refresh the retained Effect package family and source fork to 4.0.1, pinned source `460272d30457f4697d8b8c52cad41caccbcace08`. Keep `@effect/tsgo` at 0.46.1, source `f1a7cad0292d9d315e7f87694f127f605711d55e`.
- Rebase the Vite+ source fork on stable 1.0.0, source `fc287d7b1c0dc008dbc65d1d2b2f51a44e2a5ea4`, and retain its compatible Vitest 5.0.1 family. Port the Tiara integrations onto that source. Do not maintain a separate Vitest 5 backport onto the old Vite+ fork.
- Generate the scoped Vite+ package from the built, patched local Vite+ fork, not an independently installed upstream package. Build the selected core before the CLI and generated package. Regenerate the Effect helper from the 4.0.1 helper source after the scoped Vite+ test exports exist. Rewrite its runtime and type imports through `@tiara-stack/vite-plus/test`, using the stable root TestRunner API; remove stale `test/suite` and fast-check rewrites. Update executable, export, native-binding, and package checks for the 1.0.0 layout rather than assuming the old files still exist. Preserve supported lint/LSP use through the selected 1.0.0 entrypoints or the dedicated native Oxlint wrapper.
- The helper's scoped Vite+ peer lower bound must be the first scoped artifact version containing this migration and passing the consumer gates. Derive and check that lower bound against the generated package's actual version; the old 0.2.x minimum is unacceptable. Keep the Vitest compatibility range at `>=5.0.0 <6.0.0` and the Effect peer on 4.0.1-compatible releases. Assigning package release labels is implementation bookkeeping; publishing remains out of scope.
- Keep the Effect source workspace's own released development toolchain separate from the consumer runtime. Its Vitest 5.0.2 development pin need not be forced into the Vite+ 5.0.1 runtime. The installed consumer must load one runner instance through the scoped Vite+ exports. Preserve the root/core TypeScript 5.9 minimum and prove it with an installed-consumer typecheck.
- Use the stable native TypeScript 7.0.2 backend, source `2bd066d87f5bafd315be9f40889d0a60b9e58e0b`, with the 7.0.2003-derived tsgolint source `eb9339115edde6811ca94c3433adf69ea9852880`. Carry the coupled Effect/compiler and local tsgolint patches, then regenerate diagnostics and shims from the selected sources.
- Retain the approved custom Oxlint 1.87.0 source, `2bd08ebe8f36fcf1954a675ffdeb4c6d0129f609`. Effect-tsgo 0.46.1's upstream compatibility list ends at 1.85.0. The 1.87.0 port therefore requires its own bridge/protocol and consumer evidence; do not represent it as an upstream-certified pair or silently change either release pin. Provision the selected Go, Rust, and Node requirements before validation.
- Preserve the public `effect/*` rule IDs and existing configured behavior. Translate upstream `effecttsgo/*` presets and diagnostic identities into that contract. Include all 116 diagnostics, exactly 34 additions, preserve the 82 shared default severities, and carry the reviewed grouping, version support, previews, fixability, and six presets.

## Working fixes and suggestions

Forward upstream edits and suggestions through the Go adapter, native protocol, Rust bridge, and public Vite+/Oxlint result. Metadata-only fixability does not satisfy this release. Preserve the upstream distinction between automatically applicable fixes and suggestions that require explicit acceptance.

Verify a newly added fixable rule and a suggestion at the installed-consumer boundary. Check the reported identity, message, file/range, replacement text, and resulting source. Apply a safe fix through the supported public fix command; verify a suggestion includes a usable edit and that applying it yields the expected source. Rerun lint to show the resolved diagnostic disappears. Include regression coverage for a shared rule whose fixability changed.

## Implementation ownership and order

1. [Refresh the Effect source fork and dependency set to 4.0.1](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-311/refresh-the-effect-source-fork-and-dependency-set-to-401) establishes the stable Effect source, package alignment, moved imports/directories, and cache/AI regressions. [Rebase the custom Oxlint fork on Oxlint 1.87.0](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-312/rebase-the-custom-oxlint-fork-on-oxlint-1870) can start independently and carries the custom Rust integration onto the selected base.
2. After the Effect source refresh, [Align Effect-tsgo and its Effect 4 fixtures](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-313/align-effect-tsgo-and-its-effect-4-fixtures) upgrades the coupled native compiler, patches, generated shims, and fixtures. [Move the Effect test helper stack to Vitest 5](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-314/move-the-effect-test-helper-stack-to-vitest-5) owns the Vite+ 1.0.0 rebase, local-source package generation, helper regeneration, compatible peers, and single-runtime test path.
3. [Expose Effect-tsgo 0.46.1 diagnostics through tsgolint](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-315/expose-effect-tsgo-0461-diagnostics-through-tsgolint) follows native compiler alignment and owns metadata/fixture updates plus Go-side fix and suggestion propagation.
4. [Register all Effect-tsgo 0.46.1 rules in Oxlint](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-316/register-all-effect-tsgo-0461-rules-in-oxlint) follows the Oxlint rebase and tsgolint work. It owns all 116 markers, public namespace/preset translation, and Rust-side reporting and edit/suggestion propagation.
5. After the helper and native registry paths are integrated, [Verify the upgraded packages in a consumer fixture](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-317/verify-the-upgraded-packages-in-a-consumer-fixture) proves the test runtime, TS5.9 consumer, lint output, actual fixes/suggestions, and packaged binary provenance. [Add drift checks for Effect versions and lint markers](https://linear.app/tiara-stack/issue/TIA-318/add-drift-checks-for-effect-versions-and-lint-markers) checks the synchronized package baseline and exact diagnostic/marker identities in the normal validation path.

The existing native dependency graph supports this order. No new implementation ticket or replacement parent is required.

## Completion gates

- The stable Effect source workspace passes its type checks, tests, and build, including the released helper behavior and targeted cache interruption and AI regressions.
- The selected Vite+ source and scoped package build from the same patched source inputs; helper regeneration is deterministic and fails when expected rewrites or exports are missing. Its supported Node runtime and native binding versions match the chosen source release.
- Source-development commands demonstrably select repo-local Oxlint, tsgolint, and tsgo binaries after explicit overrides. Missing local builds fail clearly. Preserve the Vite lint configuration handoff; a path-only binary change is insufficient.
- The custom 1.87.0 native chain passes focused Go/Rust bridge and fixture tests and the headless smoke path. Metadata, runtime registries, markers, and presets agree on identities and established severities.
- A disposable packed consumer with no source-tree fallback passes an Effect test through `vp test`, the TS5.9 typecheck, baseline/new-rule lint checks, enable/disable and severity checks, and the working-fix/suggestion checks above. Verify rule IDs, spans, text, and actual binary/runtime selection.
- Run the target repository's lint, build, test, patch, Vite+ wiring, native build/staging, and smoke commands as applicable. Retarget version-specific patch checks to retained consumer artifacts. Run heavy checks one at a time on the shared box.

These gates are requirements for implementation; this planning effort has not passed them. If the port exposes a concrete incompatibility, report it with evidence rather than silently relaxing the approved pins or consumer contract.

## Handoff and artifacts

Add linked planning addenda to the affected existing implementation tickets, preserving their original acceptance criteria and native relationships. Their expanded Vite+ rebase and native fix-propagation responsibilities warrant the configured complex routing level.

The two cited research reports are committed locally in their isolated T3 worktrees. Graphite returned `Permission denied / EACCES`, so their requested `research/*` branch convention and Graphite tracking were not completed. The verified local report branches and commits remain in their research resolutions. No source implementation, native build/test execution, PR submission, or npm publishing is part of this completed planning decision.

The existing report commits are now also named by `research/effect-401-runtime-compatibility` and `research/effect-401-native-compatibility`, both verified as tracked from `main` with Graphite 1.8.6. Their commits, original worktrees, and source findings are unchanged. See the latest research-ticket context comments for exact branch, commit, and report paths. The research-branch naming and tracking limitation described above is closed.
